To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hydrogenase activity of E.coli transformant (pCBH6) is approximately 2-fold that of E. colic C600 (wild-type cells).

two hydrogenase genes from C. freundii were cloned into pBR322, and the recombinant plas-mid pCBH6, which contained a 2.35-kb fragment between Ava I- Eco RI sites, was found to have the highest hydrogenase activity.
the hydrogenase genes of C. freundii were cloned on pBR322.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of hydrogen from organic compounds by E. coli transformants harboring a hydrogenase gene.
the cloning of a hydrogenase gene of C. freundii and its use in E. coli.
the production of hydrogen from organic substrates by a hydrogenase gene of C. freundii cloned in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a hydrogenase gene of Citrobacter was cloned on the multicopies-plasmid pCBF2 and the recombinant plamid pCBH6 containing a hydrogenase gene and the adjacent repressor gene was constructed.
the recombinant plas-mids pCBH6 and pCBH10 were found to have the hydrogenase gene and repressor gene, respectively, of C. freundii.

the hydrogenase gene cloned on plasmid pBR32 was a repressor gene, and that the hydrogenase activity and hydrogen evolution from sodium formate were enhanced by the cloned hydrogenase gene of C. freundii.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a hydrogenase gene of Citrobacter is located in the DNA fragment between Ava I (position 2.1) and Eco RI (position 5.1) sites, which are located in the 10.7 kb DNA fragment of plasmid pBR 322, and that the hydrogenase gene of C. freundii is expressed in E. coli.
a cloned hydrogenase from C. freundii is expressed in E. coli and hydrogen production by E. coli transformants is increased.
hydrogen production was increased in E. coli containing cloned hydrogenase gene of C. freundii by reducing the size of recombinants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a recombinant plasmid pCBH4, which contains a hydrogenase gene and a repressor gene for hydrogenase, was obtained.
the hydrogen production of E. coli was enhanced by cloning a hydrogenase gene from a hydrogen-producing bacterium.
a hydrogenase gene from C. freundii was cloned in E. coli.
